picks.name: Broadcom Inc.

The Samsung-Broadcom $200B MOU signed July 26 extends the custom AI silicon pipeline through 2030, adding a new hyperscaler-quality anchor customer alongside Google and Meta. Morgan Stanley reiterated Overweight on July 27 with AVGO as a preferred AI-infrastructure expression, and the stock rose 2% on the session after last week's semi selloff — a constructive dip-buy signal. Next catalyst is the September 3 earnings print, where 48 analysts forecast $106B in FY2026 revenue, a 40% YoY improvement.

picks.name: Alphabet Inc.
picks.rationale: GOOGL is the second carry-over with the thesis firmly intact and now reinforced by the most consequential institutional endorsement of the quarter: Berkshire Hathaway nearly tripled its Alphabet stake to ~57.8M shares worth $16.6B, making it Berkshire's fifth-largest holding under new CEO Greg Abel — a quality-value stamp from the world's most scrutinized value investor. Consensus EPS revisions are tracking +18.06% over the trailing year, confirming sustained analyst confidence. The FCF negative print from $44.9B capex is a near-term quality asterisk, but capex is building the infrastructure moat that underpins the cloud backlog.
picks.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings (late October) with Google Cloud backlog conversion and Search AI monetization update
picks.entryNote: Trading at a reasonable multiple relative to the $514B cloud backlog; Berkshire's $16.6B stake establishes a valuation floor; FCF temporarily depressed by capex but guided to normalize as data centers go live; Druckenmiller exit creates counter-signal but Berkshire/Ackman exits and re-entry dynamics favor long-term holders
picks.exitTrigger: Google Cloud revenue growth decelerates below 40% YoY, or Search ad share falls more than 5pp in a single quarter from AI-native competitor disruption
picks.keyRisk: AI-native search disruption eroding core Search revenue, which is still the dominant profit driver despite cloud growth

picks.name: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.
picks.rationale: GS is the third carry-over and the strongest single-quarter earnings story on the screen: Q2 2026 EPS of $20.98 vs. $14.54 estimated (44.3% beat) on $20.34B revenue vs. $16.40B consensus, with Global Banking & Markets revenues up 53% YoY and Equities at $7.42B (+72%). ROE hit 23.5% / ROTE 25.5% — elite capital efficiency. The financials sector rotation thesis (steeper curve, reopening M&A cycle, capital markets activity driven by AI investment cycle) is in full bloom, and GS is the highest-operating-leverage expression. The yield curve's 2s10s at +37 bps with a hawkish Warsh Fed favors sustained NIM expansion and trading revenues. Financials remain one of the least expensive major sectors by forward P/E.
picks.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings (mid-October) with continued capital markets activity and potential M&A advisory fee acceleration
picks.entryNote: Post-Q2 re-rating still underway; analysts raised price targets following the 44.3% EPS beat; TBVPS growing at 10.5% annually; entering below analyst consensus target post-earnings — not yet extended
picks.exitTrigger: ROTE falls below 18% for two consecutive quarters, or a Fed rate-hike cycle crushes the M&A/IPO pipeline and trading volumes revert sharply
picks.keyRisk: A hard landing or credit event that freezes capital markets activity, reversing the record equities trading revenues

picks.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
picks.rationale: META is the fourth carry-over with the thesis unimpaired. The company reports Q2 2026 earnings on July 29 (same day as FOMC), creating a near-term binary event but also a potential catalyst for a step-change in analyst estimates. Meta's AI monetization — through ad targeting, Llama model licensing, and AI-native feed products — is the cleanest direct-monetization AI story in the Communication Services sector, distinct from GOOGL's infrastructure and cloud angle. Tiger Global significantly added to META in Q1 and it remains a top-5 holding. With advertising revenue directly correlated to consumer spending health and digital-first business formation, META's revenue is more insulated from geopolitical macro than hardware-exposed names.
picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings on July 29 with AI ad revenue contribution, Llama monetization update, and Q3 guidance
picks.entryNote: Trading at reasonable multiple for a company with 20%+ revenue growth and expanding FCF margins; Tiger Global and ARK both holding; ad revenue beat probability elevated given strong digital-ad checks from Google's Q2 beat
picks.exitTrigger: Ad revenue growth decelerates below 12% YoY, or Llama AI model licensing fails to develop into material revenue within 4 quarters
picks.keyRisk: Digital advertising cycle downturn from consumer spending pressure, or a hard regulatory ruling on data privacy forcing ad targeting restructuring

picks.name: Micron Technology Inc.
picks.rationale: MU is the fifth carry-over and the memory-cycle conviction trade. Bernstein analysts reiterated Buy on MU on July 27 citing AI-driven memory demand, alongside Morgan Stanley forecasting 25% rises in memory prices — the strongest memory pricing signal of 2026. David Tepper doubled his Micron position in Q1 13F as a concentrated bet on AI memory chip shortage dynamics; Druckenmiller also added MU. HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) is a structural bottleneck for AI GPU clusters, and Micron is one of only three companies globally that manufactures it. The sector-rotation research identifies MU as a complementary exposure to NVDA/AVGO at a different point in the semiconductor value chain — memory vs. compute — reducing single-factor correlation.
picks.catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings (late September) with HBM allocation update and DRAM/NAND pricing trajectory
picks.entryNote: Rebounded 4%+ on July 18 after Morgan Stanley memory price forecast; Tepper doubled at Q1 levels; memory upcycle historically precedes 18-month sustained margin expansion; trading at discounted forward P/E vs. logic-semi peers given commodity perception
picks.exitTrigger: HBM market share loss to SK Hynix exceeding 10pp, or AI GPU shipment deceleration that reduces HBM content-per-system demand
picks.keyRisk: Memory pricing downcycle if AI capex bubble deflates and data center build pace slows, causing DRAM/NAND oversupply relapse

picks.name: S&P Global Inc.
picks.rationale: SPGI is the sixth carry-over and the highest-quality compounder in the financials sleeve. It provides ratings, analytics, and data infrastructure that is structurally counter-cyclical — debt issuance volumes accelerate both in leveraged buyouts and in periods of refinancing pressure, which the current late-cycle environment generates. With credit markets active (Google, Amazon, Meta all issuing significant new debt to finance data-center builds), ratings revenue is directly benefiting from AI capex financing activity. SPGI's market position is a true duopoly with Moody's, and its Platts commodity/energy data segments benefit directly from elevated energy price volatility, which characterizes 2026. The financials sector remains one of the least expensive on forward P/E.
picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings (late July/early August) with debt issuance volume data and Platts energy data revenue
picks.entryNote: Trading at a modest premium to historical forward P/E but justified by structural duopoly moat; debt issuance volume in 2026 remains elevated due to AI capex financing and refinancing waves; low beta relative to pure-play financials provides quality buffer
picks.exitTrigger: Bond issuance volumes fall more than 20% YoY for two consecutive quarters, or DOJ/antitrust action that structurally disrupts the ratings duopoly
picks.keyRisk: A sharp contraction in capital markets activity (credit freeze) that collapses new ratings revenue; less likely than in prior cycles given AI-driven capex financing demand

picks.name: RTX Corporation
picks.rationale: RTX is the seventh carry-over and the defense/aerospace conviction anchor. The macro research is unambiguous: the US-Iran conflict has institutionalized elevated defense spending as a secular tailwind, and RTX — producing Patriot missiles, F135 engines, and Raytheon air-defense systems — is the most direct beneficiary within the approved universe. XLI gained 20% in H1 2026 and defense is identified as a standalone geopolitical beneficiary regardless of whether Iran tensions ease or escalate. RTX's backlog is deep and multi-year, providing revenue visibility independent of quarterly macro swings. The value category is appropriate: RTX trades at a reasonable earnings multiple for a company with government-contract revenue durability.
picks.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings (late October) with defense backlog update and GTF engine return-to-service revenue recovery
picks.entryNote: Defense sector has clear geopolitical tailwind with no credible near-term reversal catalyst; GTF engine blade durability issue largely resolved and return-to-service provides an additional revenue recovery layer; Industrials sector at near-parity with SPY YTD — not extended
picks.exitTrigger: A formal and durable US-Iran peace accord that reduces global defense procurement budgets, or GTF engine issues re-emerge at scale creating a new liability
picks.keyRisk: Defense budget sequestration risk from US fiscal austerity push under DOGE — federal spending cuts could affect procurement timelines even amid geopolitical demand

picks.name: Quanta Services Inc.
picks.rationale: PWR is the eighth carry-over and the AI power-infrastructure pick with the purest earnings visibility. Quanta provides the engineering and construction services to build the electrical grid upgrades, data center power connections, and renewable energy interconnections that AI hyperscaler capex mandates. With four AI hyperscalers projected to spend $690B+ on capex in 2026, Quanta's order book is underpinned by a decade-long secular tailwind. This is a differentiated exposure from AVGO and MU: Quanta sells picks-and-shovels physical infrastructure services, not chips — meaning it has no semiconductor demand risk and benefits regardless of which AI architecture wins. The macro brief explicitly identifies industrial and utility firms as direct beneficiaries of the AI buildout.
picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings (early August) with electrical infrastructure backlog and data center connection revenue update
picks.entryNote: XLI +20% YTD but PWR's data-center-connection backlog provides multi-year revenue visibility not yet fully priced; trades at a reasonable multiple for an infrastructure services compounder; no multiple expansion needed — backlog execution alone drives earnings growth
picks.exitTrigger: AI hyperscaler capex guidance cuts exceeding 20% aggregate, or labor/materials cost inflation compresses project margins below 10% EBITDA on new contracts
picks.keyRisk: Project execution risk: cost overruns on large-scale data center electrical interconnection projects could pressure margins and force guidance cuts

picks.name: Vistra Corp.
picks.rationale: VST is the ninth carry-over and the merchant power play on AI electricity demand. As the largest competitive power generator in the US, Vistra directly captures the power price uplift from surging data-center electricity demand — without needing to build any new AI products. The sector research identifies AI capital spending projected to add ~100bps to US GDP growth in 2026 and industrial/utility firms as direct beneficiaries of $800B+ in AI hyperscaler capex. VST's fleet of natural gas and nuclear plants provides baseload power that data centers require 24/7, unlike intermittent renewables. VST is the highest-beta pure-play electricity demand expression in the defensible-growth category, distinct from PWR's infrastructure services exposure.
picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings (early August) with power price realizations and data-center offtake contract updates
picks.entryNote: Iran ceasefire pulled natural gas prices lower, creating a short-term margin boost for gas-fired generation; nuclear baseload positioned as premium power source for AI data center bilateral contracts; trading above 52-week average but below peak — momentum intact
picks.exitTrigger: Wholesale power prices collapse more than 30% in ERCOT/PJM due to renewable overbuild, or a nuclear plant incident that forces regulatory shutdown of Vistra's nuclear assets
picks.keyRisk: Re-escalation of Iran tensions sends natural gas prices surging, compressing margins for gas-fired generation while nuclear remains constrained in output

picks.name: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc.
picks.rationale: CRWD is the tenth carry-over and the cybersecurity conviction pick. The geopolitical regime — US-Iran conflict, elevated global tensions — is the most powerful secular tailwind for enterprise cybersecurity spending, as nation-state threat actors directly target US infrastructure, financial systems, and defense contractors. CrowdStrike's Falcon platform has consolidated endpoint, cloud workload, and identity security into one AI-native architecture, creating a switching-cost moat and a land-and-expand revenue model with high NRR. The macro brief identifies late-cycle regimes as favoring quality FCF companies, and CRWD generates strong free cash flow while growing ARR well above 20% annually. The IT sector has the highest count of positive EPS guidance updates (44) in FactSet data going back to 2006.
picks.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings (late August) with ARR growth, platform consolidation wins, and FedRAMP High authorization expansion
picks.entryNote: Semiconductor volatility in July has created a sympathy pullback in high-growth tech including CRWD; July sector selloff in Nasdaq (-1.4% on week) provides a better entry than highs; cybersecurity sector spending is more defensive than discretionary tech — less cyclical drawdown risk
picks.exitTrigger: ARR growth decelerates below 15% YoY, or a second major platform outage (post-2024 incident) triggers customer churn and forces pricing concessions
picks.keyRisk: A second CrowdStrike platform outage that restores memory of the 2024 global IT disruption and triggers a customer diversification wave to SentinelOne or Microsoft Defender

picks.name: SPDR Gold Trust
picks.rationale: GLD is the #1 defensive carry-over and the highest-conviction tail-risk hedge in the portfolio. Gold spot near $4,722 (record highs) reflects a multi-year supercycle driven by central bank de-dollarization, geopolitical hedging from the US-Iran conflict, and Fed policy uncertainty — all of which are intensifying in July 2026. The bear-steepening yield curve, sticky core PCE above 3%, and potential Iran re-escalation represent gold's ideal macro backdrop. Zero earnings risk, zero credit risk, and historically low correlation to AI-equity drawdowns make this the cleanest portfolio hedge available. The 10-year yield at 4.63% with real rates near +50–70bps is modestly positive for gold given the geopolitical premium.
picks.catalyst: Iran MOU breakdown or core PCE re-acceleration above 3.5% triggering flight-to-safety demand
picks.entryNote: Near all-time highs but justified by structural demand — central banks continue buying and the geopolitical premium is not speculative; carry cost of holding gold vs. cash (4.5% T-bills) is the primary near-term headwind but offset by tail-risk option value
picks.exitTrigger: Iran conflict fully resolved with durable diplomatic accord, Fed pivots to aggressive rate cuts reducing real-rate hedging need, and central bank gold purchases reverse
picks.keyRisk: A sharp strengthening of the US dollar on risk-on sentiment (e.g., Iran peace deal + strong GDP print) compresses gold below $4,200 in the near term

picks.name: Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF
picks.rationale: SCHD is the #2 defensive carry-over and the quality-dividend compounder anchor. The ETF screens for FCF coverage, dividend growth consistency, and balance sheet strength — sectors including financials, industrials, energy, and consumer staples — while carrying far lower tech concentration than SPY or QQQ. In a late-cycle regime where 10-year yields are near 4.63%, SCHD's yield is competitive with investment-grade credit while also providing equity upside optionality. The macro brief explicitly identifies quality value with steady FCF and modest leverage as working well in a higher-rate, late-cycle environment — which is precisely SCHD's factor exposure. Low correlation to AI/semi disruption provides true diversification benefit.

picks.entryNote: Dividend yields near competitive levels vs. short-duration bonds; low P/E vs. market; defensives/value underperformed growth in H1 and represent mean-reversion opportunity if macro softens; XLP +5.0% vs SPY +18.4% — significant reversion potential

picks.keyRisk: Inflation re-acceleration forces prolonged higher-for-longer rate policy, compressing dividend equity valuations alongside bonds

picks.rationale: BRK.B is the #3 defensive carry-over and the most uniquely positioned asset in the entire portfolio. With ~$397B in consolidated cash/T-bills (approximately 59% of the combined cash + equity portfolio), Berkshire functions as a call option on market dislocations — the only mega-cap equity that benefits from rising rates through T-bill income and gets *more* attractive in crises when acquisition targets cheapen. Greg Abel's first major move — the $16.6B Alphabet acquisition — confirms disciplined capital allocation at scale. The insurance float benefits from higher rates, BNSF is a real-economy infrastructure play, and the 40 to 26 position concentration signals quality-over-quantity conviction. Near-zero correlation to pure AI momentum drawdowns.

picks.entryNote: Trades at modest premium to book but justified by cash optionality and T-bill income; Q1 portfolio concentration to 26 positions reduces noise; low beta means less upside in rallies but meaningful downside protection in corrections — appropriate for defensive sleeve sizing
picks.exitTrigger: Berkshire deploys >50% of cash reserves into a single acquisition at a price above 20x EBITDA, signaling discipline erosion under new management
picks.keyRisk: Greg Abel transition risk — if capital allocation discipline degrades under new leadership, the premium to book erodes and the defensive properties weaken

picks.name: iShares 7-10 Year Treasury ETF
picks.rationale: IEF is the #4 defensive carry-over and the duration hedge with the most asymmetric risk/reward in a slowdown scenario. The 10-year yield at 4.63% — near its 2026 YTD high — represents a meaningful entry point for intermediate duration if the late-cycle regime tips into contraction. The Fed median path implies no rate changes through early 2027 with one cut in Q2 2027; if growth disappoints on the Q2 GDP print (July 30) or PCE re-accelerates and forces Warsh to hike, IEF's price will diverge from equities — providing the cross-asset hedge the portfolio needs. Less convexity risk than TLT makes this the preferred duration vehicle at current yield levels. The Bloomberg US Aggregate fell -0.74% last week on the yield spike — creating a tactical entry opportunity.
picks.catalyst: Q2 GDP print below +1.5% on July 30, or core PCE deceleration signal that shifts FOMC language toward neutral
picks.entryNote: 10Y yield at 4.63-4.7% range (YTD high) offers the best entry in months; IEF rallied during each of the four 2026 equity drawdown episodes; medium conviction reflects dual risk that Warsh hikes rather than cuts, creating near-term duration headwind
picks.exitTrigger: Core PCE re-accelerates above 4% forcing Fed to formally restart a rate hike cycle, making intermediate duration structurally unattractive for 12+ months
picks.keyRisk: Iran MOU collapse drives oil above $100, reigniting inflation and forcing Warsh to hike in September, pushing 10Y yields above 5.0% and marking IEF positions to significant losses

picks.name: The Coca-Cola Company
picks.rationale: KO is the #5 defensive carry-over and the consumer staples anchor. Coca-Cola reports Q2 2026 earnings on July 28 (Tuesday), providing near-term fundamental confirmation. KO is the quintessential late-cycle compounder: pricing power that passes through inflation, brand equity that is genuinely global and non-replicable, consistent dividend growth history (60+ years), and a direct beneficiary of higher-for-longer rates through short-duration reinvestment of its cash flows. Consumer Staples are identified in the sector research as preferable over Discretionary in the current regime, and institutional allocators are being advised to overweight Staples for a durable earnings turnaround with recovering demand and improving margins. KO also provides direct correlation with Berkshire's core portfolio — Buffett/Abel hold KO as one of their top-5 positions.

picks.entryNote: XLP +5% vs SPY +18.4% YTD represents the most significant underperformance gap in years; KO's yield is competitive in a 4.5%-rate world but offers equity upside optionality; Berkshire holding provides institutional floor; below 5-year average forward P/E after the growth-over-value year
picks.exitTrigger: Organic volume growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters, signaling consumer trade-down so severe that brand equity is no longer defending volumes even in emerging markets
picks.keyRisk: Dollar strengthening from Iran risk-on resolution or Fed hawkishness crushes KO's substantial international revenue translation, compressing reported EPS growth

summary: The portfolio is positioned for a late-cycle regime with stagflationary friction: the Fed is on hold above neutral under hawkish Chair Warsh, core PCE is above 3%, the 3m10y has re-inverted, and the S&P 500 trades at 20.4x forward earnings — a market priced for confirmation rather than patience. The 10 growth picks express conviction in three compounding secular themes — AI infrastructure (AVGO, MU, CRWD), AI platform monetization (GOOGL, META), and the physical buildout of AI power/defense (PWR, VST, RTX) — balanced by two high-quality financial compounders (GS, SPGI) that benefit directly from a steeper yield curve and elevated capital markets activity. All 10 names are carry-overs from the prior week's book with thesis continuity intact: AVGO's Samsung MOU, GOOGL's Berkshire endorsement, GS's 44% EPS beat, META's July 29 earnings catalyst, and MU's Bernstein/Morgan Stanley memory price calls all reinforce rather than undermine prior conviction. The defensive sleeve spans gold (GLD, geopolitical/inflation hedge), dividend quality (SCHD, late-cycle rotation), a cash-fortress equity (BRK.B, optionality on dislocations), intermediate duration (IEF, GDP/PCE tail hedge), and consumer staples (KO, earnings this week). The dominant risk being underwritten is an Iran MOU breakdown driving oil back above $100, reigniting inflation and forcing Warsh to signal hikes, which would compress tech multiples, pressure IEF, and trigger a growth-to-defense rotation — partially hedged by GLD and the portfolio's existing tilt toward pricing-power and FCF-generative names.
diversificationNote: Growth book spans five GICS sectors: Information Technology (AVGO, MU, CRWD — three names, at the sector cap), Communication Services (GOOGL, META), Financials (GS, SPGI), Industrials (RTX, PWR), and Utilities (VST); the two AI-infrastructure semiconductor names (AVGO, MU) share secular demand exposure but occupy different points in the value chain (custom AI silicon vs. HBM memory), while PWR and VST represent physical infrastructure vs. power generation — complementary rather than correlated. Defensive sleeve spans gold (GLD), broad dividend/quality income (SCHD), a cash-fortress equity compounder (BRK.B), intermediate-duration Treasuries (IEF), and consumer staples (KO) — covering all four required defensive exposure categories with no duplicated exposures.
